answer: An agent economy can make each identity climb its own ridge of useful work before it may transact: a newcomer must complete a growing chain of verified tasks, each one building on the last, so the effort cannot be split across fake accounts. A relic of that chain, the record of completed work, stays bound to one identity and cannot be copied or sold. A gale of fresh fakes therefore faces the full cost of climbing every ridge again, while honest agents keep the standing they already earned.
